clue.text: After eleven alien enters some concern

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one group of letters is placed within another

blocks.note: 'some' and 'any' are interchangeable in many sentences
eleven in Roman numerals
ET, the film's extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A worried note that some extra-terrestrial has arrived just after eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After eleven' reads as a time of day, but it orders two pieces: the Roman numeral comes first and the alien after it, and that pair enters the word for 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxiety is a state of worry, and concern used as a noun means much the same unease.

clue.text: Rearrange Colt pieces to be capable of retraction and protrusion

indicators.note: to rearrange is to put things in a different order, which is just what happens to these letters

blocks.note: ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for stripping and reassembling the parts of a Colt revolver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces' looks like gun parts but is part of the fodder; Colt is a famous American firearms maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A telescopic object, like a collapsible antenna, slides its sections in and out to shorten or lengthen.

clue.text: Awful funeral song – not good

indicators.note: 'not' says something must be absent, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: a dirge is a lament sung at a funeral
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A harsh review of a dreary funeral song: awful, no good.
explanation.walkthrough: Take G out of DIRGE to leave DIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire is an adjective for something dreadful or extremely bad, a close synonym of awful.

clue.text: Quiet about wise man making forecast

blocks.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
RE means concerning, as in a letter heading
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: A hushed guru delivers a prophecy about the future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container signal, but here it is RE, simply placed in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: To presage is to foretell or give warning of a future event, which is a forecast.

clue.text: Remark about pelvis regularly getting flatter

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
'about' means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: a comment is a remark
first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A doctor's remark about a patient's pelvis that somehow ends up flattering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flatter' looks like a comparative adjective (more flat), but it is the verb to praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To compliment someone is to praise them, and to flatter is to praise them, often excessively.

clue.text: Prison unrest I resolved partly

indicators.note: 'partly' says only part of the phrase is used, so the letters sit inside it

blocks.note: running across the end of the first word into the next two

explanation.surface: A report on a prison riot that has been only partly settled.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir is old slang for prison, as in 'stir crazy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is informal British slang for jail, a place where convicts serve their time.

clue.text: Saucy uniform heads of resources brought to upset

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only opening letters are kept

blocks.note: pert means cheeky or impudent
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
initial letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Department heads are shocked when a racy uniform is brought before them.
explanation.walkthrough: Uniform is U in the radio alphabet used by pilots and armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb is to disturb or make anxious, which matches upset used as a verb.

clue.text: Deduce gold found across island is substandard

indicators.note: lying across something means stretching over it on both sides, so the outer letters straddle another

blocks.note: to infer is to deduce
I is the abbreviation for island
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A prospector concludes that the gold discovered on an island is poor quality.
explanation.walkthrough: INFER followed by OR straddles I. OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior describes something of lower quality, falling below the required level, which is what substandard means.

clue.text: Market unpopular permit

blocks.note: out of favour, as in 'flares are out'
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A trader complains about a permit for a market that nobody likes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Market' looks like a verb or an adjective-noun pair here, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlet is a place or channel where goods are sold, so a retail market for products.

clue.text: Let’s rise up with unlimited energy

indicators.note: 'up' can mean in turmoil, as when things are all up in the air, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: eight letters taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A rousing call to get up out of bed full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' alone is the anagram signal and 'rise' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tireless never flags or becomes weary, so they seem to have boundless stamina.

clue.text: Brigand put rodent in dish

indicators.note: 'put ... in' instructs placing one thing inside another
'in' completes the instruction, saying where the insertion goes

blocks.note: a rat is a rodent
a pie is a dish

explanation.surface: A bandit's cruel trick: sneaking a rat into someone's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' and 'in' together tell you to insert one piece into the other; the definition is the single first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a robber or outlaw, and a pirate is a robber who operates at sea.

clue.text: Cellists forking out for small gifts

indicators.note: 'out' can mean wrong or disordered, as a joint is put out, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Musicians paying up to buy little presents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forking out' reads as one phrase meaning paying, but 'forking' is fodder and 'out' alone stirs the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocking fillers are the little presents put inside a Christmas stocking, so they are inexpensive gifts.

clue.text: Tons unsaid about details

indicators.note: 'about' can mean turned around or moved about, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Plenty remains unspoken when it comes to the fine print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like it means concerning, but it is the signal to rearrange the ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The ins and outs of a matter are its intricacies, all the particular points and fine print.

clue.text: Inadequate Los Angeles blokes on board

blocks.note: the city's usual abbreviation
blokes is British slang for men
a table is a board, as in 'bed and board'

explanation.surface: A sniffy judgement of some Hollywood men sitting on a company board.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, one piece 'on' another sits above it. 'On board' looks like it means aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamentable means deplorably bad, the kind of poor performance that falls woefully short of what is needed.

clue.text: Jerk succeeded in plans to return

indicators.note: returning is going back the way you came, so the letters run backwards
'in' puts one thing inside another

blocks.note: maps are plans, as in a street plan
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A fool managed to get included in the plans to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' tempts as an insult for a person; here it is a sudden twitch. MAPS turns round to SPAM, and S goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is an involuntary muscular contraction, a sudden jerk of the body.

clue.text: Main setter’s disreputable

blocks.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
the setter refers to themselves, so 'setter's' is 'my'

explanation.surface: A confession that the crossword compiler's chief quality is shadiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective meaning chief; it is the old noun for the ocean, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: Seamy describes the sordid, unpleasant side of life, matching something of shady, low repute.

clue.text: I am trapped in unsuitable inverted drum

indicators.note: inverting turns something upside down, which in a down answer runs the letters backwards
something trapped is enclosed by something else

blocks.note: inapt means not suitable
contraction of 'I am'

explanation.surface: A complaint from someone stuck inside an upturned drum.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'inverted' means read bottom to top; the reversal happens first, then the contraction is slipped in after its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Timpani are kettledrums; the plural is often used for the set and loosely for a single drum.

clue.text: Hear son running to Portuguese woman

indicators.note: running suggests letters moving about loosely, so they are reordered

blocks.note: seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Listen as a boy runs over to a Portuguese lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' suggests a sound-alike clue, but it is simply part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Senhora is the Portuguese title for a married woman, equivalent to Mrs or madam.

clue.text: Caught less productive maid perhaps

blocks.note: C is caught in cricket scoring
lean means unproductive, as in lean years

explanation.surface: A domestic servant has been caught slacking at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the maid as just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is one kind of domestic worker who cleans a house, hence a definition by example.

clue.text: Ignored cyclist cycling around back of van alarmingly

indicators.note: the back is the end, so only the final letter is kept
cycling suggests letters spinning round and landing in a new order
'around' means surrounding, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: fourteen letters taken as written
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cyclist ignored by a van driver weaves around the back of it in alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' looks like part of the cycling scene, but it is the anagram signal; the shuffled letters wrap the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disconcerting unsettles or upsets you, so acting disconcertingly is behaving in an unnerving, alarming manner.

clue.text: God of love following a vote

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, so the piece named first is placed last

blocks.note: taken as written
a poll is a vote
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A deity of romance coming after an election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'God of love' wants to be the definition (Eros, Cupid); only 'God' defines, and 'love' is O, placed after A POLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo is the Greek and Roman deity of music, poetry and the sun.

clue.text: Oaf left unconscious

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
out cold, knocked out

explanation.surface: A clumsy brute has been left senseless.
explanation.walkthrough: A lout is a British word for a rough, uncouth young man.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a clumsy, boorish person, and a lout is a similarly crude, aggressive one.

clue.text: Hotel with concept and means to provide refuge

blocks.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an idea is a concept
a way is a means, as in a way of doing something

explanation.surface: A hotel with a bold concept and the resources to shelter guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' looks like money or a verb; here it is WAY, a method.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideaway is a secluded place to retreat to, so it serves as a shelter or sanctuary.

clue.text: Short dance record

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a disco is a dance

explanation.surface: A brief dance number on vinyl.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last letter from DISCO.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinyl record is a flat circular disc carrying grooves of recorded sound.

clue.text: Sense one unit changed with time

indicators.note: changed means altered, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A feeling that a military unit has been altered over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' joins the fodder before the shuffle, and only then is time added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit is to know or perceive something by instinct, which is to sense it without reasoning.

clue.text: Sorted out and replaced bottoms of shoes worn by Victor

indicators.note: what is worn is wrapped around the wearer, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: to resole is to fit new soles
V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cobbler fixed and resoled the shoes that Victor wears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottoms of shoes' looks like a first-letters signal, but the whole phrase means fitting new soles.
explanation.definitionFit: When a problem is resolved it has been settled or fixed, which is what sorted out means.
